fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Judges 13:9 says the angel of God returned to the woman as she was sitting in the field, "but her husband Manoah was not with her." The same verse says God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel returned. His prayer got answered, and he missed the front-row seat.

No servant in this scene, friend. The text says the woman herself "…ran quickly to tell her husband…" (Judges 13:10). She carries the news with her own feet. Some news you don't hand off to a messenger, and I think this was one of those.

That's right, baker. The angel says, "Even if I stay, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." (Judges 13:16). So an offering is for the LORD, not for the angel's plate. Manoah wanted to host a guest, and the angel points him to the LORD instead.

I bet that's what Manoah was hoping, friend, but the angel says otherwise. "Even if I stay, I will not eat your food." (Judges 13:16). Then he adds, "But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." So that goat is not going on the angel's plate.

Yes, baker. "When the flame went up from the altar to the sky, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame." (Judges 13:20). The text says the LORD did a marvelous thing, and Manoah and his wife looked on as it happened. That's a visit nobody forgets.

Not quite, friend. This verse has the angel going somewhere: "…the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame." (Judges 13:20). The flame goes up from the altar to the sky, and he goes up in it. Manoah and his wife look on while it happens.

True, friend. "When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell facedown to the ground." (Judges 13:20). They go down right after the flame goes up and the angel ascends in it. Both of them, and straight down. I've dropped to the floor myself, mostly when I've dropped a whole tray of dough.

Yes, baker. Manoah's wife says, "If the LORD had intended to kill us, He would not have accepted the burnt offering and the grain offering from our hands…" (Judges 13:23). She goes on to say He wouldn't have shown them all these things or spoken to them this way. Manoah brought fear, and I think she brought a calm look at what had actually happened.

No dreams in this verse, friend. The text says, "…the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol." (Judges 13:25). The verse puts a name on who does the stirring and a place where it starts. That's the Spirit of the LORD, at Mahaneh-dan.
